title: APAC Private Deployment Rollout Playbook
content:
Purpose and audience:
This working playbook is the go-to-market skeleton for the APAC launch of Redwood Private (VPC + on-prem package). Primary readers: AE/SE teams covering APAC, solutions engineering leads, partner/alliances reps, and product marketing writers preparing customer-facing collateral. Use as a living doc — copy snippets into decks, email templates, and battle cards.

Executive elevator (1-2 lines):
Redwood Private for APAC gives regulated and sensitive customers the same high-throughput, predictable LLM inference used by our hosted customers, delivered inside their VPC or on-prem footprint with KMS/HSM integrations, audit-ready logging, and enterprise SLAs.

Target segments in APAC (priority order):
- Financial services (retail banking + wealth) — strict data residency and audit trails.
- Healthcare / life sciences — PHI concerns and on-prem requests.
- Large telco platform teams — regional latency + operator partnerships.
- Public sector and education (selected pilot programs).

Primary value props to lead with (core messaging pillars):
1) Predictable performance & cost: dedicated capacity (reserved) with capacity planning and SLO-backed latencies for production LLMs.
2) Data control & compliance: customer-managed VPC pathing, KMS/HSM support, enhanced audit logs and retention controls.
3) Unified developer UX: same Redwood API and SDKs as hosted — minimal app changes during migration.
4) Enterprise operations: rollout controls (canary/A-B), tracing hooks, and Redwood Console for per-route observability.

Feature highlights (customer-facing bullets):
- VPC Private Endpoint + optional on-prem appliance for air-gapped installs.
- Seamless model pinning and versioned rollouts; automated fallback to compatible lower-cost variants.
- Key management integrations (AWS KMS / Azure Key Vault / HashiCorp + HSM options).
- Trace-level cost/latency dashboards, token-level breakdowns, and per-model quality monitoring.
- Optional managed Dedicated pools for hybrid setups.

Competitive snapshot (quick notes for SEs):
- Cloud hyperscalers (AWS/Azure/Google): strength = native infra and existing contracts; weakness = fragmented LLM developer UX, less opinionated inference optimizations and higher per-token ops complexity. Hammer: unified API + tuned runtime that reduces token $/latency.
- LLM API providers (horizontal SaaS): strength = easy dev experience; weakness = limited private deployment options or immature enterprise SLAs. Hammer: enterprise-grade private deployment + same API surface.
- Inference infra vendors (self-hosted runtimes): strength = control and cost; weakness = heavy ops + engineering lift. Hammer: managed control plane, jump-start configs, templates, and optional professional services.

Objection handling (short answers):
Q: "Why not just run open-source model ourselves?"
A: You could, but Redwood reduces months of engineering work: runtime optimizations for batching/kv-caching, pre-built kernels and quantization profiles, model onboarding assistance, and a control plane for rollouts and SLO monitoring. We measure unit-cost reduction and time-to-prod savings as part of the POC.

Q: "How do you handle data residency and audits?"
A: Private deployments can be VPC-only or on-prem. We integrate with customer KMS/HSMs, capture audit logs with configurable retention, and offer downloadable compliance artifacts for SOC/GDPR/region-specific needs.

Sales play / POC checklist (for SEs + Solution Architects):
- Pre-call: confirm infra preference (VPC vs on-prem), expected peak TPS, model families to serve, compliance/regulatory list. Link to onboarding questionnaire: https://forms.redwood.company/apac-private-poc
- Infra validation: network topology diagram, egress rules, KMS endpoints, firewall requirements.
- Baseline performance test: run Redwood micro-benchmark (script reference in linked_artifacts) using customer model or recommended variant.
- Security review: deliver threat model doc and HLD to customer security team.
- Pricing trigger: get expected sustained throughput estimate for Dedicated vs metered.

Internal enablement assets to build (owner):
- SE battlecard (Daniel Walker) — concise 1-pager with feature bullets, pricing ranges, common objections.
- Pre-sales checklist (Mina Sato) — technical questionnaire and network checklist.
- Partner pack (Carlos Rivera) — reseller-friendly value props and co-sell templates.
- APAC launch FAQ (this doc -> living).

Announcement draft (internal-first):
Subject: Launching Redwood Private (APAC) — enablement & resources\Body (starter):
Team — we’re live with our APAC Private offering for early customers. Key outcomes: 1) regionally-located Private control plane for VPC deployments, 2) on-prem appliance pre-alpha for select partners, 3) SE enablement kit ready. Please review the SE battlecard and join the 02/17 enablement call.

Customer-facing announcement (short):
Headline: Redwood Private now available in APAC — enterprise-grade LLM inference inside your cloud or datacenter.\Lead: For regulated and latency-sensitive workloads, deploy Redwood where your data lives. Reach out for a pilot.

Pricing guidance (talk tracks, not public list prices):
- Small POC: short-term metered + professional services to cover installation and onboarding.
- Pilot / Early production: reserved Dedicated pool pricing (3–12 months) to get predictable performance and a discount.
- Enterprise: annual commitments + support add-on and on-prem license for air-gapped installs.
Note: legal must approve any large discounts for APAC region — route through finance before committing.

KPIs to track first 90 days: (report cadence: weekly for first 6 weeks, then bi-weekly)
- Number of APAC POCs started and % converted to paid pilot.
- Avg latency and token cost for APAC private instances vs hosted baseline.
- Number of security signoffs completed (customer audits passed).
- SE enablement reach: number of AEs/SEs trained, enablement call attendance.

Sample customer email (short template):
Hi <Name>,
We can deploy Redwood inside your VPC to keep data in-region and meet your audit requirements. Can we schedule a short technical scoping call next week? I’ll bring our solutions architect to discuss KMS integration and performance targets.

Open questions / risks (action owners):
- On-prem appliance beta readiness: what is the exact feature set for the initial pilot? (Owner: infra product)
- Local partner agreements required for APAC on-prem installs in country X? (Owner: Partnerships)
- Legal/regulatory: any country-specific data export language needed for contract? (Owner: Legal)

Next steps (near term):
1) Finalize SE battlecard and publish to Confluence (target 2025-02-20).
2) Run internal enablement webinar (live demo) 2025-02-24.
3) Field first 5 POC requests from pipeline and iterate on onboarding checklist.

Notes to self / drafting log:
- Keep messaging heavy on control + parity with hosted API — engineers want minimal code churn.
- Avoid deep model-architecture claims in customer-facing material; focus on operational outcomes (latency, cost savings, reliability).
- Follow-up: add short one-page technical HLD template to linked_artifacts.

End of playbook (living) — feedback welcome.
